chapter: Recording dates, Goodman and band life
title: Why he did not join Benny Goodman in 1944 and the Mildred Bailey show
summary: Teddy Wilson recommended him, but Jones stayed in New York with the Stuff Smith Trio, which had just done Mildred Bailey's CBS show.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: How long did you work with him?
Just during the few weeks that I was off and Sarah was off, that's all, you know. But I was supposed to go with him immediately after I got to New York with Stuff Smith.

I wanted to stay there and get my card and get my own little reputation. And we were going back to Chicago, you know, and Teddy Wilson was -- I think he was going to teach at Julliard at that point, you know, and he recommended

me. Because we had done the Mildred Bailey show in the radio days, you know, with the trio. We were getting booked all over the place. On CBS, you know, and NBC and all those places, and we just happened to hit it, if I can put it that way, you know? The timing was right, a unique trio, a violin, bass and piano, playing jazz. No drums or nothing, you know, just -- we were very fortunate that way. And I think it was a wise thing that I didn't go with Benny Goodman. And I just wanted to stay in New York and expand in that direction.
Let's see, was it her radio show? It was her radio show. She had a big radio show in those days, on CBS, you know?
